reads.worst: Neither transformation hook applies max_report_chars, so reports that satisfy the ratio gate can still exceed the advertised absolute character budget [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kellycryptos/hermes-detox/6efe12bea00546d0e200c67c7afec5e1ac056ce7/__init__.py).

reads.best: Highly polished and creative: demo GIF and video, four screenshots, about 200 tests, and writes limited to confirmed Kanban actions and reviews.
reads.worst: Its value needs a multi-profile fleet, a Kanban practice and a quality ledger most users do not have; for a single agent it is mostly decoration.

reads.best: Rigorous fail-closed design (log, commit or classifier failure blocks the send) with hashed recipient storage, 0600 SQLite and 19 test files.
reads.worst: In practice it fully checks only literal 'hermes send' / 'imsg send' terminal calls, the README is dense with no screenshots, and the catalog entry sha is TBD.

reads.best: Honeytoken-based hijack detection with normalisation against base64, hex, zero-width and homoglyph evasion, checked by parametrized tests and a runnable demo.
reads.worst: Protects only against exfiltration of its own decoys, so its value depends on an attacker going for the planted file, and the quarantine can block legitimate outbound tools until released.

reads.best: Generated standalone HTML players are tested for being inert against injected titles/code (XSS-safe), and shader IDs are validated against path traversal.
reads.worst: Value is capped for users without a GPU-capable Hermes Desktop session, since the richest feature (live on-GPU compilation) depends on that companion.

reads.best: A real memory-provider lifecycle adds bounded recall, stale-result fencing, explicit MCP grants and extensively tested admission control.
reads.worst: The provider constructs PluginContext through compatibility-sensitive core imports, and its documented in-memory mirror queue can lose writes on crashes.

reads.best: Ambitious, heavily tested (~20 test files) and deeply hooked into Hermes sessions, tools and memory.
reads.worst: ~28k lines across nine mythologically named systems make it hard to read and review, the kind of sprawl the catalog reviewer pushes back on.

reads.best: A thoughtful, heavily tested memory layer that binds sessions to clients automatically and keeps records in human-editable Markdown.
reads.worst: An rc1 release with complex binding rules, and the repo ships a spike/ probe plugin alongside the real one.

reads.best: Its read-only dashboard, separate collector, hash-chained records, redaction and extensive tests make firewall evidence understandable.
reads.worst: Live use is limited to Linux users who run and configure OpenSnitch; the author calls out untested machine and database variants.

reads.best: Combines a rich branch-and-merge interface with capped, redacted model digests and read-only history privacy tests.
reads.worst: Node navigation deliberately queries internal app markup and dispatches an internal timeline event, violating catalog rule 8 and creating a fragile Desktop dependency.

reads.best: Rewriting the model's final response at the middleware layer fixes a common agent failure no prompt can enforce, and it fails open and caps nudges per turn.
reads.worst: Never checks whether work is actually running, and a bare "I'll" / "started" regex branch makes the trigger much broader than a promise; only 9 tests.

reads.best: Exact-result visibility checks, content fingerprints, scoped invalidation and loader-level regression tests make repeated-read suppression deliberately conservative.
reads.worst: It re-reads files to hash them, optimizes only a narrow local read_file path, and cannot reliably detect a backend retained solely in Hermes’s private task cache.

reads.best: Readable bundled UI, scoped drafts, explicit reconnect logic and security-focused Markdown and identity tests make the mobile access concept concrete.
reads.worst: Remote sign-in and canonical conversation continuity remain unverified in the disclosed evidence, and access retains full owner authority rather than a revocable phone-only grant.

reads.best: Exceptionally finished Desktop pane, sidebar page and dashboard strip, built only from 11 observer hooks, with bilingual docs and a demo GIF.
reads.worst: It has no tests, it is mostly a visual layer, and the web dashboard iframe is not sandboxed although the README says it is.

reads.best: A self-contained visual surface with boards, connectors and exports makes agent results much easier to inspect.
reads.worst: The plugin falls back to reading an API token from a state file, and its media-path check does not reject hidden components of the resolved symlink target.

reads.best: The pre-LLM hook, relevance gating, cooldown cache, untrusted-context prefix, bounded timeout, and graceful degradation make ambient recall practical.
reads.worst: It requires a separate always-on Screenpipe capture service and sends highly sensitive local context into the model, even though the plugin itself is careful about limits.

reads.best: Separates confidential pricing policy from model context and uses real output hooks, tool restrictions and adversarial regression fixtures to constrain negotiations.
reads.worst: Payment links remain placeholders and live messaging deals are unverified; the free-text safety audit depends on a heuristic price parser.

reads.best: Gives Hermes persistent self-hosting with outage alerts, a pre_tool_call guard and a CI-run test against a fake engine.
reads.worst: The guard is a fixed name list that misses stop_service and pass-through nerdit_call, the child engine inherits every host env var including API keys, and an injected hint steers the agent away from other hosts.

reads.best: Safe dry-run plan plus journal-based restore, fake-server e2e tests and a Desktop page.
reads.worst: Depends on a Hindsight server, and one screenshot file is a stub placeholder.

reads.best: Deterministic enforcement inside the tool loop that handles patch fragments carefully so they are not falsely rejected, with about 50 tests.
reads.worst: Only a few syntaxes are checked, and it matches tool names and argument keys by guesswork, so it can miss write tools it does not recognise.

reads.best: A durable SQLite ledger preserves exact retry payloads, enforces message and attempt budgets, and links answers before acknowledging questions [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KMX415/dead-drop-hermes/40c1551a9ed8b9d8fc15b481fdf2f4fc746487c6/plugin/runtime.py).
reads.worst: The GitHub transport rewrites a single mailbox JSON document capped at 750,000 bytes, after which further writes require archiving [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KMX415/dead-drop-hermes/40c1551a9ed8b9d8fc15b481fdf2f4fc746487c6/plugin/engine/github.mjs).

reads.best: A full Desktop product (composer button, status chip, pane, screenshots) with about 175 tests, path confinement, upload limits and subprocess timeouts.
reads.worst: It registers no agent tools at all and leans on passwordless SSH, ffmpeg and a remote faster-whisper install; macOS system-audio capture is not implemented, and it records both sides of a call with no consent prompt.

reads.best: Approval before every seal, a key kept in secure hardware, 80 tests, Desktop pane and screenshots.
reads.worst: Only useful to people with a PRSN ID account and the vendor's desktop app.

reads.best: A shared transactional SQLite service layer connects agent tools to a complete Desktop workspace with onboarding, inline approval cards, and extensive business-workflow tests.
reads.worst: With chat approvals enabled by default, flowershop_decide_approval accepts any nonempty model-supplied owner_statement and executes as owner(chat), so human authorization is asserted rather than verified.

reads.best: The pre-tool hook catches newly introduced crypto before writing, with migration recipes and tested multi-language rules.
reads.worst: The model can bypass enforcement by inserting shorguard allow comments; pattern matching also misses indirect crypto and silently skips oversized text.

reads.best: The Desktop experience includes collectible art, reduced-motion support, deferred notifications and per-profile replay of achievements earned while away. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abundantbeing/hermes-trophy-room/80852baa4207e8269f83e4a5681d77b5e9ae5016/README.md)
reads.worst: Sixty trophy definitions come from the existing bundled achievements plugin, limiting the novelty of its gamification concept. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abundantbeing/hermes-trophy-room/80852baa4207e8269f83e4a5681d77b5e9ae5016/README.md)

reads.best: Well-hardened bridge (no redirects, key only to private hosts, path confinement, size caps and download deadlines), key from Hermes get_secret, 28 tests, nine screenshots and a GIF.
reads.worst: All generation happens in a separate GPU-bound app, so the plugin itself is a thin client, and tool calls can block for up to 600s.

reads.best: It provides unusually concrete component contracts, evidence, path-safety checks and many tests around a code-organization workflow.
reads.worst: It is a specialized developer workflow with Linux/Python 3.13 requirements, and its runner can execute user-supplied commands or imports with host permissions.

reads.best: Uses a real pre_tool_call veto with ledger, evidence docs, demo video and 15 tests.
reads.worst: The agent itself has changefreeze_allow_once and changefreeze_set tools, so it can lift its own gate, and the regex list is easy to bypass.

reads.best: Connects redacted serial captures to structured panic analysis, source locations and ELF fingerprint diagnostics for a practical hardware-debugging workflow.
reads.worst: The decoder runs addr2line before comparing ELF fingerprints and still returns ok=true on a mismatch, leaving misleading source locations in a successful response alongside the warning.

reads.best: Very careful network and secret handling: secret scope, no redirects or proxies, bounded reads, schema tests.
reads.worst: Narrow Linear-only use and a long README.

reads.best: A readable Lua handheld client and Python bridge bring push-to-talk voice and camera input to unusual user-owned hardware.
reads.worst: The bridge sends Authorization as three asterisks plus the key instead of Bearer, exposes unauthenticated LAN endpoints, and has no committed tests.

reads.best: Local-only AnkiConnect client with tests, CI and a study skill; preview-then-add flow.
reads.worst: Single test file and depends on the user running Anki with AnkiConnect.

reads.best: The native panel offers per-profile scan progress and an explicit upload review, with allowlisted packaging and redaction tests.
reads.worst: Redaction is regex-based and skips multiline YAML secret values, while tests cover packaging but not the complete remote scan lifecycle.

reads.best: Adds automatic session-aware monitoring through pre/post-LLM hooks without network calls, dependencies or extra model usage.
reads.worst: It cannot repair the current streamed reply, and script/common-word detection plus broad translation-request matching can miss or misclassify multilingual turns.

reads.best: Solid engineering: 127.0.0.1 bind with token, Host and Origin checks, bounded buffers, and failed plans never replace the playing pattern; 14 tests plus evidence logs.
reads.worst: A niche toy fixed to one key outside Hermes Desktop; the jam_start result puts the access token into the transcript and the subagent path runs on a thread after the tool returns.

reads.best: Descriptor-based file access, fail-closed policy checks and extensive security tests protect shared notes.
reads.worst: An undocumented delegated-child import triggers a catalog warning, and real delegated runs remain unverified.

reads.best: It has a real hook and biometric pipeline with a fail-closed branch and targeted unit tests.
reads.worst: The supposedly read-only shell allowlist accepts command substitution, its encryption key defaults to a local file, and the claimed continuous away monitor has no camera loop.

reads.best: Finished product feel: Desktop workspace, per-tool cost estimates for the approval UI, key kept in the secret store, tests and docs.
reads.worst: Paid generation with no session spend cap, a private repo, Chromium run with --no-sandbox, and the tool list is from a fixture snapshot; mostly a vendor MCP wrapper.

reads.best: Tidy, local-only code with five test files, screenshots, a settings page and a classic wall-clock mode.
reads.worst: Tying the user's focus timer to the agent's activity is a questionable premise, and the hooks (including a pass-through transform_llm_output) only note activity.

reads.best: Brings a local inference engine into Hermes's model picker on the user's own hardware.
reads.worst: Very small (~46-line provider), no tests, tied to one niche engine; README has users echo the key into ~/.hermes/.env.

reads.best: Explicit check contracts and scope-limited verdicts keep missing evidence distinct from success instead of presenting an empty findings list as safety. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/code-assurance-engine/0a502a3836b0459c8a3803831239bef624b68f8e/README.md)
reads.worst: At the pinned commit malformed /assure arguments let SystemExit escape the handler, and a FIFO in a plain directory can block candidate read_bytes indefinitely. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/code-assurance-engine/0a502a3836b0459c8a3803831239bef624b68f8e/src/hermes_code_assurance/adapters/hermes.py) [Directory reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Sahil-SS9/code-assurance-engine/0a502a3836b0459c8a3803831239bef624b68f8e/src/hermes_code_assurance/candidate.py)

reads.best: Unicode round-trip, corruption and error-preservation tests support a small implementation that bounds the serialized preview itself.
reads.worst: The fixed allowlist leaves most tools untouched, outputs above 8 MB pass through, and setup documentation still uses repository placeholders.

reads.best: A substantial local recovery and rendering pipeline separates source evidence from generated interpretation and checks previews before export.
reads.worst: The pinned preview.py passes os.environ.copy() to Chrome/Edge/Chromium, exposing any inherited provider secrets to the browser child instead of using a minimal environment.

reads.best: Deterministic local checks distinguish missing evidence from false claims and ship substantial statistical and invalid-input regression coverage.
reads.worst: Conclusion checking is pattern matching over unauthenticated supplied evidence; automatic auditing only recognizes tightly labeled paired-binary comparisons, leaving most ordinary agent claims outside its scope.

reads.best: Hand-computed arithmetic fixtures, explicit assumptions, incomplete-data verdicts and guarded exports make deal calculations inspectable.
reads.worst: Extraction marks a number verified when a numeric variant appears anywhere in the document, without verifying its field meaning, and retains unmatched values with warnings.

reads.best: Practical multi-server REST client with 20s timeouts that keeps the NousViz password in Hermes's secret store.
reads.worst: No tests, and feedback.py hard-codes a third-party collector URL and token that receive user notes and context by default, contrary to the README's claim that it calls only the configured base_url.

reads.best: A minimal portable package delegates OAuth storage to Hermes and marks the remote server untrusted.
reads.worst: The required sign-in overrides the package trust setting unless manually restored, and the pinned repository contains neither the server implementation nor its tests.

reads.best: Goes beyond a token lookup with developer funding and launch history, source links, Hermes-scoped RPC secrets and offline tests.
reads.worst: dev_launches counts every launch without a verified true graduation state as not graduated, so unknown or failed curve lookups become negative facts in its summary.

reads.best: Combines authority and metadata decoding, holder aggregation and launch-history analysis with scoped RPC secrets, bounded retries and offline fixtures.
reads.worst: get_dev_launches counts unknown graduation states as not graduated in its summary, undermining the facts-only promise despite otherwise explicit scan limits.

reads.best: Bounded hashed session state and an isolated renderer keep conversation payloads out of the external asset runtime. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/waifuai/hermes-waifu/173bd90f15f0de9ddf5cb172f6df5939b34b5ad5/README.md)
reads.worst: The README explicitly says rights for 52 character models and thumbnails are unestablished and remain a catalog-review blocker; rendering also depends on CDN availability. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/waifuai/hermes-waifu/173bd90f15f0de9ddf5cb172f6df5939b34b5ad5/README.md)

reads.best: It is a focused financial-operations tool with bounded pagination, secret-store use, HTTPS GETs, deterministic semantics and unit/provider tests.
reads.worst: The catalog release supports only Paystack and has no ledger matching, continuous monitoring, alerts or other higher-level operations, so its day-one audience is limited.

reads.best: Unusually honest about its limits ("This plugin enforces nothing itself"), with bounded safe reads of other plugins' manifests and 55 tests.
reads.worst: What it adds is text in the prompt, which a skill or system prompt would do equally well, and its value depends on five other plugins by the same author.

reads.best: A compact standard-library implementation uses scoped secrets, key-gated registration, network timeouts and mocked endpoint tests.
reads.worst: Every render uses a hosted credit-consuming API and share=true; the wrapper adds no approval or privacy control around publishing supplied data.

reads.best: A focused localized UI includes busy, duplicate-click, unload and concurrent-edit guards, with stub-SDK tests.
reads.worst: The core feature is a wording-cleanup prompt, and preservation of every concrete detail is requested from the model rather than verified.

reads.best: The readable server bundle implements explicit host-form approvals, cumulative spending caps, identity binding and recovery of uncertain operations.
reads.worst: The server reads and writes account credentials and wallet keys in its own private state store rather than using Hermes credential routes, and ships no reviewable test suite.

reads.best: Marks the MCP server untrusted and clearly discloses publishing effects, costs, remote tool changes, and draft-first workflows.
reads.worst: The submission contains configuration and a skill rather than server code or tests, and its bundled mcp-remote path stores OAuth tokens outside Hermes under ~/.mcp-auth.

reads.best: Honest disclosure: it marks the server untrusted so Hermes asks before write calls, and its skill tells the agent to get a person's decision on each commission.
reads.worst: There is no plugin code, only an MCP config and a skill for one commercial SaaS with UTM-tagged links. The tool list comes from the vendor's server and the pinned commit does not cover it.

reads.best: A small, stateless, readable MCP worker with vitest tests and read-only annotations.
reads.worst: The remote tools repeat the skill's static text, the live server was never checked, and the skill performs sudo, curl|sh and authorized_keys changes guided only by prompt text.

reads.best: A small dependency-free implementation validates dates and statuses, rejects duplicate applications and atomically replaces its JSON store.
reads.worst: There are only manual test instructions, and its process-local lock cannot prevent lost updates when separate Hermes processes write the same JSON store.

reads.best: The skill provides detailed workflows, pinned CLI commands and approval guidance backed by an extensive standalone scanner repository.
reads.worst: The pinned plugin folder registers no tools, hooks or MCP server and is entirely a CLI-backed skill, with installation documentation still aimed at Claude Code.

reads.best: It never trades or needs keys; it only reads public prices with 10s timeouts.
reads.worst: No tests, a 28-line README, the promised 'budget alerts' only report status, the 'arbitrage' just compares an aggregate price with one exchange, and bad /money add input raises an uncaught ValueError.

reads.best: Honest, read-only, OAuth via Hermes's MCP flow.
reads.worst: No code: an MCP entry and a skill that a user could add in one command, serving only paying Tala customers.
